title: Encarnación merchants and commerce employees march for a border subsidy
location: Roundabout in front of the Entidad Binacional Yacyretá offices, Nueva Esperanza neighborhood, Encarnación
organizer: Coordinating group of merchants from the new commercial circuit; no formal organization named
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. ABC Color announces a “great demonstration” but gives no attendance. Counts for shops, affected workers, or prospective subsidy beneficiaries are not protest turnout.

title.summary: The pre-event story announces the demonstration; same-day reporting confirms that merchants and commerce employees marched.

start_date.summary: Same-day reporting dated 20 January confirms the march occurred on the scheduled date, starting after concentration outside EBY offices; exact start time is not stated.

end_date.summary: The report says participants decided to maintain a vigil at the bridge entrance; it does not establish departure, dissolution, or the physical end.

location.summary: The pre-event story names the EBY-office roundabout; same-day report says people gathered outside EBY and marched through the new commercial circuit, then decided to maintain a vigil at the bridge entrance.

scope.summary: The reported march and vigil are in Encarnación; no other sites are described for this episode.

organizer.summary: The pre-event report identifies the circuit merchants’ coordinating group; the same-day story describes merchants and employees without naming a new organizer.

demands.summary: The planned action was to pressure Paraguay’s Senate to approve an economic-subsidy bill; no provided category directly represents this demand.

participants_original.summary: The source describes a “nutrido grupo” (substantial/sizable group) but provides no numerical count.

participants_min.summary: No explicit numerical lower bound is provided; “nutrido grupo” does not establish 50 people by itself.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Occurrence is confirmed, but the only turnout wording is “nutrido grupo”; it gives no count or clear evidence of at least 50 participants.

protester_violence.summary: Pre-event article does not report event conduct; violence remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The article reports a planned vigil while waiting for the Senate but no event-specific state reception, refusal, or coercive response; all seven dimensions remain unknown.

eligibility.summary: A public march occurred and its state-subsidy demand is documented, but the >=50 threshold remains unsupported by “nutrido grupo” alone.

notes: Same-day ABC Color reporting confirms that merchants and commerce employees marched through the Encarnación commercial circuit and decided to maintain a vigil at the international-bridge entrance. This is occurrence evidence but remains one publisher and no numerical turnout is given. Demand is for state subsidy approval; the original demand taxonomy mapping is unresolved.
open_questions: Did the gathering reach the 50-person threshold?
Was the reported vigilia physically maintained after the article and for how long?
Did any state reception or response directly address the march?
Does the demand map to an original category after the official Coding Procedure is available?

title: IPS resident and contracted doctors’ 4 January assembly / announced strike lead
organizer: IPS resident and contracted doctors; formal organizer not identified
participants_original: Attendance at the assembly is not reported.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The assembly report gives no attendance count or qualitative 50-plus estimate. Workforce figures and the reported 70 contract terminations are not protest turnout.

title.summary: The opened ABC Color article reports an assembly of resident and contracted IPS doctors and a planned strike; it does not establish that the assembly was a public protest.

start_date.summary: The opened article published 4 January says the doctors held an assembly that morning. This is the reported assembly date, not a confirmed date for a qualifying public protest.

end_date.summary: The article does not report the assembly’s physical end or departure/dissolution.

location.summary: The assembly’s venue is not established in the reviewed article. The separate reports placing mobilizations outside Hospital Central do not establish where this assembly occurred.

scope.summary: The article does not establish whether the assembly was open to the public or an internal labor meeting.

organizer.summary: The article identifies resident and contracted doctors as holding the assembly but does not identify a formal organizing body.

demands.summary: The article links the assembly and announced strike to 70 terminations and removal of seniority credit for residency years; labor-dispute mapping is provisional.

participants_original.summary: No assembly attendance is reported. Figures about terminated doctors and the resident/former-resident workforce describe affected workers, not people present at this assembly.

participants_min.summary: No attendance lower bound is reported; workforce figures are not turnout.

participants_max.summary: No attendance upper bound is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No attendance count or qualitative 50-plus description is reported for the assembly. Workforce totals and terminations cannot establish 50 attendees.

protester_violence.summary: The article provides no event-specific conduct sufficient to code protester violence; unknown.

state_response.summary: The article does not document an event-specific state response to the assembly; all seven dimensions remain unknown.

eligibility.summary: The 4 January assembly itself is reported, but its public/open status, venue, and turnout are not established. Separate sources document outside-IPS mobilizations on 3–5 January (E004), but do not establish whether this assembly is the same episode or relates continuously to the pre-January stoppage context (C001). Keep pending_evidence.

notes: This record preserves an assembly that ABC Color reports occurred on 4 January and a related future strike announcement. It is not evidence that the assembly was public/open, reached 50 people, or qualified as a public protest. Keep it separate from E004’s reported outside-IPS mobilizations while the relationship remains unresolved; neither merge nor treat it as an added attendance count. The January date is the reported assembly date; its relation to the older-onset C001 stoppage series and January unit ownership of any broader physical episode remain uncertain. Conflicting planned strike dates do not establish strike execution or a physical end.
open_questions: Where did the assembly occur, and was it open to the public or an internal labor meeting?
How many people attended; did the gathering reach 50?
Was the assembly physically separate from E004’s 3–5 January outside-IPS mobilizations, or part of the same sequence?
What is its relationship, if any, to the pre-January stoppage context in C001?
What were the assembly’s physical end and any event-specific state response?
Did either announced strike date lead to a separate physical action?

title: IPS resident and contracted doctors mobilize outside Hospital Central, 3–5 January
location: Outside Instituto de Previsión Social / Hospital Central, Asunción
organizer: IPS resident and contracted doctors; formal organizing body not consistently identified
participants_original: Reports refer to groups of doctors; no attendance count reported.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. No attendance count or clear qualitative 50-plus description was reported; affected workforce counts are not turnout.

title.summary: Contemporaneous reports describe resident/contracted IPS doctors’ outside mobilizations and staggered stoppages on 3–5 January.

start_date.summary: Outside mobilizations are dated 3 January (S014), 4 January (S015/S016), and 5 January (S011); the series was already underway by 31 December (S019). The physical onset and whether the January gatherings form one episode with earlier activity are unresolved, so start_date is null.

end_date.summary: Reports cover gatherings/stoppages through 5 January and future strike plans. Calling off an 8 January plan or describing another planned date does not establish the physical end of the observed gatherings.

location.summary: Reports place mobilizations outside IPS / Hospital Central in Asunción.

scope.summary: The reports describe local gatherings at the IPS/Hospital Central site; no other site is established for this candidate.

organizer.summary: Resident and contracted IPS doctors are identified; a formal organizer is not consistently named.

demands.summary: Doctors sought recognition of residency years as labor seniority and opposed contract terminations; this is a labor dispute involving the state social-security institute IPS.

participants_original.summary: Sources refer to groups of doctors but provide no attendance number.

participants_min.summary: No explicit attendance lower bound. Figures for 51 renewed contracts and 200/300 residents refer to staff/workforce, not turnout.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count or clearly 50-plus qualitative description is reported; threshold remains unproven.

protester_violence.summary: Inspected reports do not provide event-specific conduct sufficient to code violence; unknown.

state_response.summary: An IPS meeting and officials’ statements about contracts/seniority are reported, but no field-specific state-response code is assigned from silence or unspecific negotiation; all seven dimensions remain unknown for these gatherings.

eligibility.summary: Actual public mobilizations outside the state IPS site are reported, but turnout is not enough to establish 50 and the physical onset/relationship to pre-January stoppages is unresolved; pending_unit.

notes: A January candidate for the actual outside-IPS gatherings, not the internal/publicity-uncertain 4 January assembly lead E003. La Nación on 31 December reports that staggered stoppages were already continuing, while 3–5 January reports document outside mobilizations. Do not force a December-to-January merge or a fresh January onset: physical onset/episode boundary remains unresolved. The separate 7 December protest is not presumed continuous. The planned 8 January strike was reported called off; a HOY-reproduced IPS statement mentions a different 11–13 January plan. Neither plan establishes execution or the gatherings’ physical end.
open_questions: When did the physical episode begin, and are Jan 3–5 gatherings continuous with the Dec 31 stoppage series or distinct new actions?
Did at least 50 people attend?
What was the physical end?
Did state authorities directly accommodate or respond to the outside mobilizations?
Did the planned Jan 8 or Jan 11–13 strike occur?
